Q: Why is freeze panes causing error 1004 when workbook is minimized? A:

.FreezePanes works only on the active window, and Excel cannot freeze panes in a minimized workbook window. When TestNew is minimized, ActiveWindow is either Nothing or pointing to a different window, so Excel throws Run-time error 1004.

Also, you don’t need to maximize the window. Setting it to xlNormal is sufficient. I’d recommend checking the current window state and then restoring it to either xlNormal or xlMaximized as appropriate.

Option Explicit

Sub Sample()
    Dim wb As Workbook
    Dim ws As Worksheet

    Set wb = Workbooks("TestNew")
    Set ws = wb.Sheets(1)

    '~~> Ensure the workbook window is usable
    With wb.Windows(1)
        If .WindowState = xlMinimized Then .WindowState = xlNormal
        .Activate
    End With

    ws.Activate

    '~~> Freeze panes without ambiguity
    '~~> Replace 5 with rowA8_Start code
    ws.Cells(5, 1).Select
    ActiveWindow.FreezePanes = True
End Sub

Q: How to set a relative path in HTML? A:

The easiest way to solve this in pure HTML is to use the <base href="…"> element like so:

<base href="http://localhost/mywebsite/" />

Then all of the URLs in your HTML can just be this:

<a href="images/example.png">Link To Image</a>

Just change the <base href="…"> to match your server. The rest of the HTML paths will just fall in line and will be appended to that.

Q: Does the linker option -Wl,-rpath-link=dir need to be given for all the necessary library dependencies search paths? A:

no need to link all transitive dependencies, -Wl,-rpath-link is only needed so the linker can find dependencies of the libraries you directly link, since libd.so links only to libc.so the linker just needs help finding libb.so, libb.so already knows about liba.so, so libd.so doesn’t need ../a, but your second command is closest

if you are building the libs yourself you might want to embed the rpath

Q: Apps Script or Contextual Gadget to add UI to Gmail A:

Its not correct that "nobody except the developers of those services have permission to access the interface" since you can write gmail contextual gadgets, however those only show in the body of a received email and not on the new message window.

Can't be done with apps script either which does allow you to create web interfaces (not just for processing data) but you cant add them to the gmail window.

Best option is to write a browser extension and cover the case of gmail/inbox browser pages.

Q: How do I fix the jupyter notebook search box error "TypeError: can't access property "length", child is undefined"? A:

There is such an easy fix to this that I had to share this. I came to think of fixing this only after many of these error messages since the notebook is huge and I could not spend the time on it.

Clip the whole cell and then, the error is gone at once, without leaving and opening the session.

You can then paste the same cell from the clipboard at the same place, and the whole writing can be seen and edited again, and the search box error does not pop up again.

Thus, it must have been a copy and paste error from copying right from the chatbot output. My guess: a space sign that is forbidden in markdown. Or something else that makes the text more than a text or a broken text. That would also go with the Error "TypeError: can't access property "length", child is undefined".

Q: How do I make HELO publish an SPF record? SPF_HELO_NONE - SPF: HELO does not publish an SPF Record A:

I was able to get rid of the warning by adding an extra TXT record with the name "www" to the www.mailserver.com DNS:

mailserver.com
Name    Type    Value
@       A       1.2.3.4
*       A       1.2.3.4
@       MX      10 mailserver.com.
@       TXT     v=spf1 ip4:1.2.3.4 ~all
www     TXT     v=spf1 ip4:1.2.3.4 ~all <-- adding this record fixed the warning
